+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Cases for the claims orca.nix makes about the Orca CLI and its agent skills:
+# that `orca-ide` and `orca` are the CLI and run from any shell, not only an
+# Orca terminal, and that the skills in ~/.claude/skills are the bytes this
+# Orca build expects.
+#
+# Why this needs a test. Orca's own installer only reaches an Orca terminal: it
+# puts a shim dir on PATH there (ORCA_CLI_BIN_DIR) and symlinks
+# ~/.local/bin/orca-ide at a raw /nix/store path, which outside the FHS env is
+# an Electron binary looking for the host's libraries. The skills are stubs
+# that tell the agent to run `orca-ide skills get <name>`, so a skill without a
+# working CLI is a dead end. And the skills are pinned to a commit separately
+# from the AppImage version; bumping one without the other silently installs
+# guides for a different CLI. Orca ships the expected hashes in
+# resources/skills/current-manifest.json, so that is what the files are held to.
+#
+# Usage:
+#   tests/orca-cli-skills.sh    eval + build this host's config and test it
+
+set -u
+set -o pipefail
+
+fails=0; n=0
+pass() { n=$((n+1)); echo "ok   $1"; }
+fail() { n=$((n+1)); echo "FAIL $1: $2"; fails=$((fails+1)); }
+
+FLAKE=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)
+# uname -n, not /etc/hostname: Orca's sandbox does not bind the latter in.
+HM="$FLAKE#homeConfigurations.$(uname -n).config"
+SKILLS="orca-cli orchestration computer-use orca-per-workspace-env orca-linear linear-tickets"
+
+pkg_attr() { # pkg_attr <pname> <attr>
+  nix eval --raw "$HM.home.packages" \
+    --apply "ps: (builtins.head (builtins.filter (p: (p.pname or \"\") == \"$1\") ps)).$2"
+}
+drv=$(pkg_attr orca-cli drvPath) || { echo "no orca-cli in home.packages here" >&2; exit 1; }
+want_version=$(pkg_attr orca-cli version) && [ -n "$want_version" ] \
+  || { echo "orca-cli has no version" >&2; exit 1; }
+CLI=$(nix-store --realise "$drv" | tail -1) || { echo "could not build orca-cli" >&2; exit 1; }
+gui_drv=$(pkg_attr orca drvPath) || { echo "no orca in home.packages here" >&2; exit 1; }
+GUI=$(nix-store --realise "$gui_drv" | tail -1) || { echo "could not build orca" >&2; exit 1; }
+echo "testing $CLI and $GUI"
+
+# The skills' own rule: outside an Orca terminal, on Linux, the CLI is
+# `orca-ide`; elsewhere it is `orca`. Both names must be the CLI, and the GUI
+# must not also claim `orca-ide` -- in the profile it would shadow one of them.
+for b in orca orca-ide; do
+  if [ -x "$CLI/bin/$b" ]; then pass "orca-cli provides bin/$b"
+  else fail "bin/$b" "missing from $CLI"; fi
+done
+if [ -x "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" ] && [ ! -e "$GUI/bin/orca-ide" ]; then
+  pass "the GUI is orca-ide-app and leaves orca-ide to the CLI"
+else fail "GUI bin names" "$(ls "$GUI/bin" | paste -sd' ')"; fi
+
+# Run from an Orca terminal, this test is already inside the GUI's FHS env, so
+# a bare wrapper exec'ing the Electron binary would pass every case below.
+# Hold the launcher itself to being a bwrap one.
+if grep -q bwrap "$(readlink -f "$CLI/bin/orca-ide")"; then
+  pass "the CLI runs in its own bwrap FHS env"
+else fail "CLI launcher" "$CLI/bin/orca-ide does not exec bwrap"; fi
+
+# `orca open` spawns the app; without ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE that is the raw
+# Electron in the CLI's env, with no wayland flag, fonts or nixGL.
+app=$(grep -o -- '--setenv ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE [^ ]*' "$(readlink -f "$CLI/bin/orca-ide")" | awk '{print $3}')
+if [ -n "$app" ] && [ -x "$app" ] && [ "$(basename "$app")" = orca-ide-app ]; then
+  pass "orca open launches the wrapped GUI ($app)"
+else fail "ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE" "'${app:-unset}' is not an orca-ide-app"; fi
+
+# The manifest travels with the extracted AppImage, which the CLI's runScript
+# references, so it is in the CLI's closure.
+contents=$(nix-store -qR "$CLI" | while read -r p; do
+  [ -f "$p/resources/skills/current-manifest.json" ] && echo "$p"; done | head -1)
+[ -n "$contents" ] || { echo "no extracted AppImage in the closure of $CLI" >&2; exit 1; }
+manifest="$contents/resources/skills/current-manifest.json"

     8	  # worktree. Closed-source Electron app, not in nixpkgs (nixpkgs' `orca` is
     9	  # the GNOME screen reader), so this packages the official Linux AppImage.
    10	  # The electron-updater feed in each GitHub release, latest-linux.yml, is
    11	  # the source of truth for version + sha512 when bumping: the yml's sha512
    12	  # is the AppImage's, checked against
    13	  # the download with `nix hash to-sri --type sha512 <sha512sum>`.

    22	  # Wrap the AppImage (not autoPatchelf of the .deb) so the Electron stack
    23	  # runs in appimageTools' FHS env, which works on non-NixOS hosts. Electron
    24	  # safeStorage wants libsecret at runtime.
    25	  orca = pkgs.appimageTools.wrapType2 {
    26	    inherit pname version src;
    27	    extraPkgs = pkgs: [ pkgs.libsecret ];
    28	    # The sandbox gets its own fontconfig, the way every other nix GUI app here
    29	    # gets a nix-generated FONTCONFIG_FILE, instead of the distro's.
    30	    # buildFHSEnv binds the host's /etc/fonts in, assuming NixOS; Arch's conf.d
    31	    # links point into /usr/share/fontconfig, which the sandbox's /usr replaces,
    32	    # so all of them dangled and every family fell to Montserrat Thin. See
    33	    # fontsConf below. tests/sandbox-fonts.sh.
    34	    extraBwrapArgs = [ "--setenv FONTCONFIG_FILE ${fontsConf}" ];

    36	    # install makes `orca-ide` the CLI, and Orca's skills tell agents to run
    37	    # exactly that outside an Orca terminal, so `orca-ide` is orcaCli below
    38	    # and the GUI is `orca-ide-app`, which the desktop Exec and
    39	    # meta.mainProgram use. appimageTools keeps the AppImage's own bin name,
    40	    # so the wrapper is renamed by hand.
    41	    #
    42	    # --ozone-platform=wayland: Orca's startup gate picks X11 when neither
    43	    # --ozone-platform nor ELECTRON_OZONE_PLATFORM_HINT says otherwise, and on
    44	    # a Hyprland-only session there is no X server to stat — measured: the
    45	    # bare launch exits 1 with "needs a usable display server", and the
    46	    # explicit wayland switch keeps it running (timeout kill at 20s, exit 124).
    47	    # An env var would work from a shell but not a desktop-file launch, so it
    48	    # is a flag on the command line.
    49	    #

    51	    # buildFHSEnv, whose buildCommand short-circuits genericBuild's phase
    52	    # list, so postFixup never runs. The bin/orca symlink from buildCommand
    53	    # is replaced with a wrapper that prepends the flag and passes "$@"
    54	    # through. buildFHSEnv's builder has no makeWrapper on PATH, so its setup
    55	    # hook is sourced by hand; and the wrapper must not target its own path
    56	    # (wrapping a renamed launcher in place makes it exec itself), so the
    57	    # bwrap launcher moves aside to .orca-ide-unwrapped.

    74	  };

# Cases for the claim that orca's sandbox resolves fonts the way the host does
# -- the claim orca.nix's extraBwrapArgs make.
#
# Why this needs a test. Orca runs in appimageTools' bwrap FHS env, and
# buildFHSEnv bind-mounts the *host's* /etc/fonts into it, on the NixOS
# assumption that its conf.d links point into /nix/store. On Arch they point
# into /usr/share/fontconfig, and inside the sandbox /usr is the env's own, so
# all of them dangle: no sans/sans-serif/Arial/system-ui aliases at all. Every
# family Chromium asks for then falls to the first font in sort order --
# Montserrat Thin, from the google-fonts set -- and the whole UI rendered in a

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Why: invoked via ~/.local/bin/orca-ide symlink (from CliInstaller); resolve it
# so APP_DIR points at the real install, not the symlink's parent.
SOURCE="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
while [ -h "$SOURCE" ]; do
	DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$SOURCE")" >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd)"
	SOURCE="$(readlink "$SOURCE")"
	[[ $SOURCE != /* ]] && SOURCE="$DIR/$SOURCE"
done
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$SOURCE")" >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd)"
RESOURCES_DIR="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd)"
APP_DIR="$(cd "$RESOURCES_DIR/.." >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd)"

# Why: Linux executableName is `orca-ide` (avoids Ubuntu GNOME Orca conflict);
# `-f` rejects a same-named directory that `-x` alone would accept.
ELECTRON=""
for candidate in orca-ide orca Orca; do
	if [ -f "$APP_DIR/$candidate" ] && [ -x "$APP_DIR/$candidate" ]; then
		ELECTRON="$APP_DIR/$candidate"
		break
	fi
done

if [ -z "$ELECTRON" ]; then
	echo "Unable to locate the Orca executable next to $RESOURCES_DIR" >&2
	exit 1
fi

# Why: Orca packages the CLI entrypoint outside app.asar so the public shell
# command can execute it directly with ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE, mirroring the same
# launcher model used on macOS instead of maintaining a separate Node binary.
CLI="$RESOURCES_DIR/app.asar.unpacked/out/cli/index.js"

export ORCA_NODE_OPTIONS="${NODE_OPTIONS-}"
export ORCA_NODE_REPL_EXTERNAL_MODULE="${NODE_REPL_EXTERNAL_MODULE-}"
unset NODE_OPTIONS
unset NODE_REPL_EXTERNAL_MODULE

# CLI commands run in Electron's Node mode and must never initialize Chromium.
ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 exec "$ELECTRON" "$CLI" "$@"

## NO EMAILS

**Never write an email address into anything.** Not into files, commit messages,
docs, notes, handoffs or scratch files — mine, colleagues', or service accounts.
This repo is public, and an address is a durable identifier that spreads: it
leaks the work/personal boundary, it enumerates people, and once written it gets
copied onward.

Refer to an account by its **role** — "the personal Google account", "the work
account", "the project's GCS service agent" — or record the command that
recovers the identity at read time (`gcloud config get-value account`) rather
than pasting its output. Role-based wording is better documentation anyway: "must
be the personal account, not the work one" survives an address change; a pasted
address does not.

If an address seems genuinely load-bearing, ask first.

The exception is the git identity already configured in `home.nix`, which git
requires and which is on every commit regardless.

## Commit and Push Policy

This is a personal dotfiles repo on `master`. When asked to commit and push, do both without asking for confirmation. The global "ask before public communications" rule does not apply here.

## Applying config: use `hms`, not `home-manager switch`

`hms` (defined in `home.nix`, documented in `README.md`) pushes, waits for the
commit's CI run on `forge.ko.ag`, then switches — so the switch is a download of
the closure the in-cluster runner built, not a local compile. Expect it to block
for ten-odd minutes. `hms --local` builds here instead.

It refuses on a dirty tree and on a checkout behind `origin/master`. **Both
refusals are the feature.** CI can only build a pushed commit, so do not route
around them with a bare `home-manager switch` — commit and push, or pass
`--local` deliberately and say that you did.

If a run goes red, `hms` prints the job's `error:` lines; read those rather than
re-running blind. Background on why CI is worth waiting for — and the 600s attic
transfer ceiling that made it unreliable for its first 61 runs — is in
`docs/ci-nix-home.md`.

## Round 2 review of `2f5d3162..HEAD` (orca.nix, tests/orca-cli-skills.sh, tests/sandbox-fonts.sh)

I built nothing new. I checked the comments and test parses against the store paths the flake already has: the CLI bwrap launcher `/nix/store/p7lwr0d1…-orca-cli-1.4.238-bwrap`, the extracted AppImage `k0m448kg…-extracted`, the skills fetch `g2wc6v5x…-orca-skills-e6f7…`, and nixpkgs at `/nix/store/REDACTED`.

### Critical
None.

### Important

**1. tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:29 — the new test cannot run in CI.**
- `HM=…homeConfigurations.$(uname -n)…` goes against the convention the CI runner relies on. `.forgejo/workflows/nix-eval.yml:152-165` handles the container hostname problem by writing `$TEST_HOST` into `/etc/hostname`, and every other test uses `cat /etc/hostname` (hyprland-graceful-exit.sh:36-43, claude-main-edit-guard.sh:25-28, sandbox-fonts.sh:37, and others).
- Under `hmeval --ci tests=tests/orca-cli-skills.sh`, `uname -n` returns the container ID. That is exactly the "does not provide attribute 'homeConfigurations.328998cea6c4…'" failure the workflow comment describes.
- The reason the test gives (Orca's sandbox does not bind `/etc/hostname`) is true; `/etc/hostname` is absent here. But it should be a fallback, e.g. `host=$(cat /etc/hostname 2>/dev/null || uname -n)`, not a replacement.
- The same fallback is needed in sandbox-fonts.sh:37, which still uses `cat /etc/hostname` and so fails inside an Orca terminal. The diff touches that file but leaves this line alone, so the two tests now disagree.

**2. tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:103 — `python3 -I` is not in CI's tool shell.**
- The CI shell provides bash, coreutils, gnugrep, gnused, gawk, git, jq and diffutils (nix-eval.yml:173-176). There is no python.
- Without python3, `want` comes back empty and all six skill cases fail with the misleading message "manifest wants 'no entry'".
- The repo uses jq for this everywhere else (zed-modular.sh, hyprland-graceful-exit.sh, brotli-cve test). Suggested replacement: `jq -r --arg n "$s" '.skills[]|select(.name==$n).files[]|select(.path=="SKILL.md").exactSha256' "$manifest"`.

**3. tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:64-67 — the ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE case does not check what it claims.**
- The pass message says "launches the wrapped GUI". The orca.nix comment (lines 111-113) explains this is about the nixGL, wayland-flag and fonts wrapper. But the test only checks that the path exists, is executable and is named `orca-ide-app`.
- The unwrapped `orca` derivation also has `bin/orca-ide-app` (the makeShellWrapper output). So changing orca.nix:121 from `${orcaGui}` to `${orca}`, which drops nixGL, still passes.
- `$GUI` is already the nixGL-wrapped package from home.packages, so the fix is to compare exactly: `[ "$app" = "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" ]`.
- Separately, nothing actually runs `orca open`. The "honours this override and strips ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE" claim is true in upstream code (`out/cli/runtime/launch.js` and `orca-app-executable.js` read `ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE` and call `stripElectronRunAsNode`), but the test only checks it statically. Acceptable if intended; the pass message overstates it.

### Nits

- **orca.nix:100-101:** "`orca` (what they run inside one…)". Inside an Orca terminal, `~/.config/orca/linux-orca-cli-shim/orca` comes before `~/.nix-profile/bin` on PATH, so the shim wins and this package's `orca` only serves "elsewhere". Wording overclaims slightly.
- **orca.nix:156-159:** the whole skill directory is a store symlink. home.nix:2176-2185 links skills file by file (`…/SKILL.md`). The comment at 136-139 justifies the choice, so this is a style difference only. No clobber conflict exists today: `~/.claude/skills` has none of the six.
- **tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:30:** `SKILLS` copies `orcaSkills` from orca.nix. Removing a skill from orca.nix fails the test (good). Adding one, or the home.file set growing, is not checked. Deriving the list via `nix eval … home.file --apply 'attrNames'` filtered on `.claude/skills/` would close that.
- **tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:58:** `grep -q bwrap` matches any mention of "bwrap", including the launcher's own comment text ("mounting one via bwrap", line 117 of the launcher). A tighter match is `grep -qE '/bin/bwrap$'` or `exec "\$\{cmd`.
- **tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:88:** `grep -q '^# '` accepts any markdown heading. Comparing against the SKILL.md / bundled-guide title would be stricter. Low risk.
- **tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:94-108:** only SKILL.md is hashed. That matches today's manifest (every one of the ten entries lists only `SKILL.md`), but a skill that later gains files would be partly checked. Iterating `files[]` would avoid that. The exit status of `nix-store --realise "$srcdrv"` (line 101) is ignored, but the hash check still catches a failed fetch ("missing"), so no false pass.
- **orca.nix:95-98 vs 7-93:** comment density and style match the existing blocks (why-first, measured claims, cross-references to tests). No issue.

### Verified as accurate
